name: Ductus - Letter Tracing Generator for Latin, Cyrillic and Greek
summary: Generates letter tracing lessons from your own font in Latin, Cyrillic and Greek: 177 glyph lessons with authored stroke order, designed plates and a runtime tracing board.
description:
Ductus generates letter tracing lessons from your own font, in Latin, Cyrillic and Greek.

Ductus carries the one thing a font cannot tell you, the order and direction a letter is written in, and takes the letterform from whatever font your project already uses. Pick a font, pick a script, and you have 177 tracing plates that match your game.

WHAT YOU GET

177 glyph lessons: Latin A to Z, a to z and the figures (62), the full Russian alphabet including the two Io letters (66), and alpha to omega including the final sigma (49).
341 authored strokes, each in the order and direction a child is taught to write it. No font file records that, so it cannot be read off an outline. It is written out, once, per glyph.
Font fitting: the strokes are warped onto your font's own letterforms, and every glyph is graded fitted, approximate, or fell back. You see the survey before you export anything.
Designed plates: ruled paper, a letter-shaped track to keep the crayon inside, a dashed centre guide, numbered start dots and a direction arrow at every turn. Six colourways (Candy, Meadow, Ocean, Sunny, Berry, Slate), any plate size up to 2048.
A stroke demonstration that writes the letter at constant pen speed, with a pen nib, at any moment you ask for.
A runtime tracing board for mouse and touch that raises events when a stroke lands, when the glyph is finished, and when the child goes the wrong way (wrong order, wrong direction or off the path).

WHY THE GRADES ARE IN FRONT OF YOU

Fitting a stroke skeleton to a real letterform is not always possible, and a generator that pretends otherwise hands you a confident wrong path. A single-storey ɑ is not the double-storey a a child is taught, and a heavy display face is not a handwriting model. Ductus says so, per glyph, and falls back to its own canonical form so the lesson is still correct even when it no longer matches the face. On a plain text face, 164 of the 177 lessons grade fitted, measured in a blank project against Unity's own built-in font.

YOUR FONT, YOUR LICENCE

Ductus ships no fonts. It reads yours at edit time and draws pictures of letters, so your font's own licence governs the sheets you export; a font under the SIL Open Font License is safe for this. Ductus never copies, embeds, subsets or redistributes any part of a font file.

GETTING STARTED

1. Import the package. Everything lands under Assets/CSAF/Ductus/.
2. Open Assets/CSAF/Ductus/Demo/DuctusDemo.unity and press Play. Trace the letter with the mouse, starting on the dot marked 1 and following the arrows. Go the wrong way and the board writes the letter for you, then lets you try again.
3. Open Window > CSAF > Ductus, drop a dynamic font into the Font field and choose a script.
4. Press Survey this font. Every letter is fitted and graded; click any letter to see its plate and the numbers behind its grade.
5. Pick a folder, tick which grades to include, and press Export. You get one PNG per letter.
6. To put a lesson in your own scene, add a SpriteRenderer and the CSAF > Ductus Tracing Board component to a GameObject, set Character, and press Play.

Stroke order is a teaching convention and conventions differ; the corpus is plain, readable data you can change. Punctuation is not covered: letters and the figures 0 to 9 only.
technical:
Features: 177 glyph lessons across Latin, Cyrillic and Greek with strokes in the taught order and direction; 341 authored strokes; font fitting onto your own font with a per-glyph grade; designed tracing plates in six colourways, any size up to 2048; stroke-by-stroke demonstration; runtime tracing board for mouse and touch with stroke, completion and mistake events; editor window with a fit survey and PNG export.

Number of C# scripts: 14. Visual Scripting graphs: 0.
Assemblies: CSAF.Ductus.Runtime (all platforms), CSAF.Ductus.Editor (Editor only), CSAF.Ductus.Demo (demo scene).
Editor window: Window > CSAF > Ductus. Demo scene: Assets/CSAF/Ductus/Demo/DuctusDemo.unity.
Unity version: built and tested on Unity 6 (6000.5). 2022.3 is not claimed as tested.
Render pipelines: Built-in, URP and HDRP. Plates are drawn in software into a Texture2D, with no shaders and no render textures.
Target platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, WebGL.
The font survey needs a graphics device (not in -nographics batch mode); plate drawing does not.
No Resources folder, no package dependencies, no fonts.
No third-party assets are included.

Documentation: Assets/CSAF/Ductus/Readme.md in the package, and https://github.com/onefreeman1337/csaf-releases/blob/main/docs/ductus-letter-tracing-generator/README.md
ai:
All of the C# in this package was written by an AI coding agent (Anthropic Claude) under human direction. That covers the stroke corpus, the font fitter, the software rasteriser that draws the plates, the tracing board, the editor window and the demo scene.

The plates the package produces are not made by an image model. They are drawn in code from an authored stroke corpus, plain data you can read and edit, warped onto outlines read from your own font. The gallery images are composed from plates rendered by the package. The cover image is an AI-generated illustration.

No audio is included, because the package contains no audio of any kind. Text and dialog: no.
